For me, all my thought is a pseudo-dialogue. I don't ever talk to myself. I never "work through" problems in my head or "search around" for an answer. Nearly all of my thinking is done completely abstractly or through a "conversation." Obviously, there's the usual anticipatory conversations, but my brain goes beyond that. When I explore ideas my brain conjures up someone who is relevant and would be interested in the idea; not to get information from, though, just to talk at. The reason I call is a pseudo-dialogue is because I'm not entire sure the person ever responds in an "audible" way. I think I just get the response. But I do say things like "well, yeah, but also..." and "Uhh, not really - it's more like..." and such. As such, my ideas flow at the rate I speak. Even now I am literally saying this to a literal person (as far as my brain is concerned) - albeit a generic filler person. I'd say I have not many, but definitely multiple distinct generic people for different situations and contexts, but they have tangible consistent qualities.

Reading is essentially the opposite of my thinking experience. When I read I hear a voice and never reply except maybe to chuckle to myself when something is funny, etc; but still there are two entities present. So again, I read at the pace I speak. This is the reason I don't read books. I prefer audiobooks to give me more brainpower to create imagery and emotion. And since they're not any slower, and keep me on track (I tend to drift off in my thoughts when I read) it's an all around winning scenario. When I read messages from friends I hear it in their voice, with real inflection (probably often inaccurate.) If it's someone I know very well I can even pick up on their mood based on how they reply, what words they use, how they punctuate, etc. In situations where I don't have a voice I again use generics who, again, have tangible consistent qualities. Additionally, when I read my own writing I listen to the same voice I speak while thinking. Sometimes I modify how I inflect words based on hearing me say it and not liking it.

I just thought about the fact, too, that it's only ever one other person. I might have a vague sense of other people being able to hear what I'm saying, such as if I was talking to an emulated teacher, for example. Also, it's probably worth noting that I don't "see" these people (nor myself.) At best they are sort of... figmented clouds.

Singing songs I've written is probably the only conscious flow in my head where I'm alone. Indeed, it is identical to how I feel when I sing out loud. Literally everything just falls away. And when I (my own songs) in my head I have really strong physical expression, too - especially with my larynx.

Tl;dr - I "talk" to persons and "listen" to persons in my head; I'm basically never alone.
